title: Conditional Rendering Practice
summary: Practice exercise: turn one login form into either a Login or a Register form depending on a userIsRegistered variable that must stay in App. Solved by passing the flag down as a prop, using a ternary for the button text and && for the optional Confirm Password input.

concepts.heading: Scenario
points: A variable userIsRegistered lives in App and models the result of checking credentials: true means the user exists (show Login), false means they do not (show Register).
Register mode needs an extra Confirm Password input (type the password twice); Login mode shows only Username and Password.
Constraint: the variable must not be moved out of App, so the Form component needs to receive it another way.

concepts.heading: Step 1: pass the flag as a prop
points: In App, render <Form isRegistered={userIsRegistered} />. The prop name is chosen freely; the value is the variable inside curly braces.
Conditional rendering in React is very often driven by props handed down from a parent.
In Form, accept props and read props.isRegistered.
(Extra) Data only flows downward: Form can read props.isRegistered but cannot change userIsRegistered in App. Changing it from a child comes later with state and callback props.

concepts.heading: Step 2: button text with a ternary
points: Inside the button's children use curly braces: {props.isRegistered ? "Login" : "Register"}.
Without the braces the expression is shown as plain text instead of evaluated.
Toggling the variable in App between true and false flips the label.
(Extra) Only the text node inside <button> needs to change, so the ternary can return plain strings; the element itself stays the same in both modes.

concepts.heading: Step 3: Confirm Password only when registering
points: Use && so the input is rendered only when the user is not registered: {!props.isRegistered && <Input type="password" placeholder="Confirm Password" />}.
The first version compares explicitly (props.isRegistered === false &&); the shorter form negates with !, which flips a boolean and reads as 'is not registered'.
A ternary with null in the false branch gives the same result but is longer; && is the most compact option.
(Extra) When the right-hand JSX after && spans more than one line, wrap it in parentheses so the expression is parsed as one unit.
(Extra) ! converts any value to the opposite boolean, so !props.isRegistered is true when the prop is false (and also when it is missing/undefined).

code_examples.caption: App passes the flag down
Form.jsx: ternary for the button text, && for the extra input

task.name: Login / Register form switch
task.starting_point: Forked sandbox with App holding userIsRegistered and a Form component that always renders username, password, confirm password and a Register button.
task.goal: Without moving userIsRegistered, show Login text and hide Confirm Password when it is true; show Register and the Confirm Password field when it is false.
steps: In App.jsx leave var userIsRegistered = true; where it is and render <Form isRegistered={userIsRegistered} />.
In Form.jsx accept props in the function signature (function Form(props)).
Replace the button's fixed text with {props.isRegistered ? "Login" : "Register"} inside the <button type="submit">.
Wrap the Confirm Password input in {!props.isRegistered && ( ... )} so it only renders when the user is not registered (first try props.isRegistered === false &&, then shorten it with !).
Flip userIsRegistered in App between true and false and check both screens.
task.expected_result: true: Username, Password, Login button. false: Username, Password, Confirm Password, Register button.

pitfalls: Forgetting curly braces around the conditional, so it appears as literal text.
Trying to move the variable instead of passing it as a prop.

The reference repo puts the components in src/components, uses a Button component and switches the whole <Button text=...> in a ternary rather than just the text, and renders the Username field as a raw <input> while the others use <Input>. The notes' solution follows the lecture's simpler version.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (playground data only covers sections 1-11, 14, 15).
gaps_and_ideas: Add as the closing practice task of the proposed 'Conditional rendering' lesson: starter App.jsx holds var userIsRegistered and a Form that always shows Username, Password, Confirm Password and a Register button.

Tasks: (1) pass the flag as an isRegistered prop without moving it; (2) switch the button text with a ternary; (3) hide Confirm Password with !props.isRegistered &&; (4) bonus: change the heading above the form to 'Welcome back' / 'Create an account' with a ternary.
Interactive demo: a 'registered?' checkbox that flips the prop, showing the rendered form next to the JSX with the active ternary branch and the && guard highlighted.
